messages:
maria: Quick check — alpha bakeoff finished on Llama-variant (2B/7B) sweep. Posting notes + packaging recs. :memo:

jason: saw the CI summary link, glancing now. any large regressions?

maria: overall FP8 and AWQ kept accuracy within tolerance on convo-eval and named-entities. GPTQ had 0.6–1.4% MRR drop on rerank tasks for 7B, INT8 was noisier on long-contexts (~2.2% on convo-eval). details in the table below.

sasha: can you paste the delta table? saves me opening the csv.

maria: sure — short table from bakeoff-ci (rounded):

```text
model | quant | CONVO_MRR_delta | RERANK_MRR_delta | token_latency_ms
7B    | fp8   | +0.1%           | +0.0%            | 12.5
7B    | awq   | -0.2%           | -0.1%            | 11.2
7B    | gptq  | -1.1%           | -1.4%            | 9.6
7B    | int8  | -2.2%           | -0.9%            | 8.8
2B    | fp8   | +0.0%           | +0.0%            | 6.1
2B    | awq   | -0.1%           | -0.2%            | 5.8
```

liam: nice. latency gains for GPTQ/INT8 are real but quality delta for 7B gptq is borderline.

maria: agree. proposed acceptance rule we used in bakeoff: any config with CONVO_MRR_delta <= -0.8% AND RERANK_MRR_delta <= -1.0% triggers manual review. That flagged 7B-gptq.

ananya: we should include a per-profile 'signal_weights' vector so downstream consumers can tune for latency vs quality automatically. e.g. {'latency': '0.4', 'mrr': '0.6'}.

sasha: strongly +1 for signal_weights. also add a small 'stability_score' (0..100) computed from bootstrap runs — helps rollout decisions.

maria: implemented that in prototype qmanifest. example package manifest we want in Optimize registry:

```json
{
 'qprofile_name': 'qv2.s3-awq-L',
 'base_model': 'redwood/llama-7b-v2',
 'format': 'awq',
 'opt_level': 'L',
 'compat_models': ['llama-7b-v2','llama-7b-aarch64'],
 'signal_weights': {'latency': '0.35','mrr': '0.65'},
 'stability_score': '78',
 'quality_guardrails': {'convo_mrr_drop_pct': '0.8','rerank_mrr_drop_pct': '1.0'},
 'fallback_chain': ['fp8','awq','cpu-int8'],
 'rollout': {'canary_pct': '2','auto_bump_window_days': '7'},
 'consumer_tags': ['low-latency','convo-safe'],
 'evaluation_artifacts': ['s3://optimize/registry/qv2.s3-awq-L/run_summary.json'],
 'deploy_hint': {'min_gpu_mem_gb': '12','preferred_instance': 'a100-40gb'}
}
```

jason: naming conv: qv=quant-version, s=stability-tier, opt-level short code. That looks compact.

liam: question — how do we encode multi-run stats (median, pctl95) in the manifest? we need p95 latency and median MRR.

maria: plan: keep heavy stats in the registry as separate artifact (regression_delta.csv + run_summary.json). Manifest has pointers: 'evaluation_artifacts': ['s3://...']. We don't bloat the manifest.

devex-bot: CI bakeoff job 4392 completed: https://ci.redwood.ai/bakeoffs/4392/results

ananya: packaging CLI idea: redwood-optimize package --profile qv2.s3-awq-L --eval-artifact run_summary.json --out qpkg which outputs a signed qpkg.zip with manifest + artifacts.

sasha: include a small 'deploy_hint' field for infra: e.g. {'min_gpu_mem_gb':'12','preferred_instance':'a100-40gb'} — helps Dedicated/Private match resources.

maria: yes. also adding automatic fallback policy so runtime can route to next-best variant if latency SLO breached.

liam: rollout strategy suggestion: start canary 2% for 24h with automated quality checks against production prompt set (sampled), if delta < thresholds after 24h, increase to 10%, then 50%.

jason: small ops ask — add machine-readable 'consumer_tags' in manifest so product can pick profile by tag (e.g., 'low-latency','prod-safe').

maria: added in prototype: 'consumer_tags': ['low-latency','convo-safe']

ananya: for publishing, CI should sign and produce a semantic qprofile id: qpkg:qv2.s3-awq-L+sha256:abcdef... so consumers can pin exact artifact.

maria: good call. final action items:
- maria: push qmanifest prototype to repo and add bakeoff->registry upload in CI (this week)
- sasha: add stability_score calc (bootstrap runs) to bakeoff job (this sprint)
- liam: implement auto-checker for canary bump (infra ticket)
- jason: write short doc for Optimize on how to consume signal_weights & consumer_tags

maria: ping @devex-bot when you have the PR and I'll attach the step-by-step.

devex-bot: noted. filing checklist item: OPT-4321 (qprofile packaging + registry upload) :white_check_mark:

sasha: tiny follow-up — do we want to expose per-prompt-class deltas in run_summary? helps product owners decide.

maria: yes, include per-cohort deltas (e.g., long-context vs short, rerank vs convo). We'll add cohort labels to the run_summary schema.

ananya: awesome. this should keep Optimize recommendations actionable for downstream runtime.

maria: thanks all — closing thread. will post PR link once CI is wired. :rocket:
